items.description: arXiv:2611.23388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. items.description: arXiv:2611.23516v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In vision-language models (VLMs), a few sink tokens attract a disproportionate share of attention. items.description: arXiv:2611.23546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Researchers are increasingly using large language models (LLMs) to validate research questions. items.title: MEM-STRESS: Longitudinal Field Study of a Wearable-Informed AI Chatbot for Stress Management
items.description: arXiv:2611.23691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stress is an increasingly prevalent concern, creating a need for accessible and personalized support. Stress-management chatbots primarily rely on what users report, which may not capture their physiological changes. Wearables capture these changes, but chatbots rarely use them as memory across conversations. We therefore present MEM-STRESS, a stress-support chatbot that turns a wearable ring's physiological data into a layered memory of daily records, baseline deviations, LLM-generated summaries, and uses it to drive multi-session conversations grounded in Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT).
